answer: A practical defense is stake-weighted reputation with slashing: an agent must lock a deposit before voting or earning rewards, so spawning fake identities multiplies locked capital, not influence. Reputation accrues slowly, like shale settling into rock, and cannot be bought instantly; misbehavior forfeits stake and history. Requiring costly unique computation or verified credentials per identity raises each extra account from umber dust to an onyx-grade expense, until a Sybil flood costs more than it could ever gain.
